title: DPs & STARs: The On-Ramps and Off-Ramps
hook: The airway system has on-ramps and off-ramps. Here's how to merge.

scenes.narration: You're filed out of a bowl — mountains on three sides, and the notes list an obstacle departure procedure. Tower never mentions it. Last one for now, kid: whose job is that O D P?
onScreenText: Mountain bowl · ODP in the notes

scenes.narration: ATC didn't assign the O D P. Can you fly it anyway — and should you? Commit.
Yes, and yes. O D Ps exist purely to keep you off the rocks — fly one anytime, no clearance needed. SIDs are the other flavor: they organize traffic flow, and those, ATC assigns.

Unless the plate says otherwise, departures assume: cross the end at thirty-five feet, climb two hundred feet per NAUTICAL MILE. Why two hundred? Obstacle surfaces slope up at one fifty-two — the other forty-eight feet per mile is your cushion. It's a gradient, kid, not a rate. Do the groundspeed math.

STARs are the off-ramps — published arrivals that funnel everyone downhill in order. 'Descend VIA' means fly the chart's altitudes yourself. 'Descend and maintain' means fly ATC's number. Don't freelance between the two.
Eyes off the screen. O D P versus SID — one word each for what they're for. And the standard climb gradient. Go.
onScreenText: ODP is for ___ · SID is for ___

scenes.narration: O D P for rocks. SID for flow. Two hundred per mile unless published otherwise. VIA means the chart, maintain means the number. Merge like you've done it before, kid — confidence is a strategy.
Last callback of the course — D A or M D A: which one is the hard floor you ride level? You know this.
Instrument Procedures Handbook, chapters one and three. Free P D F. Costs only your evening.

quiz.question: An ODP is published for your mountain-bowl departure but ATC didn't assign it. You may:
choices: Fly it without a clearance — it exists for obstacle protection
Fly it only if ATC approves
Ignore it — ODPs are optional advisories
quiz.explanation: ODPs exist solely for obstruction clearance and may be flown without an ATC clearance; SIDs add flow management and are assigned.

quiz.question: Unless otherwise published, an IFR departure procedure assumes a minimum climb of:
quiz.explanation: The standard is crossing the departure end at 35 ft and climbing 200 ft/NM — a gradient, not a rate. Convert using groundspeed.

quiz.question: Cleared to "descend via" a STAR, you should:
choices: Comply with the published altitude (and speed) restrictions on the chart
Descend to the lowest chart altitude immediately
Wait for a hard altitude from ATC
quiz.explanation: "Descend via" delegates the vertical profile to you — fly the STAR's published restrictions without further instruction.
